scenes.title: Non-Clustered Index
scenes.narration: A non-clustered index is a separate lookup structure that points back to the rows without dictating their physical order.

scenes.title: How it is built
bullets: It stores the indexed key plus a locator back to the row
The locator is a row address or the clustering key
A table can have many non-clustered indexes
scenes.narration: A non-clustered index stores the indexed key values alongside a locator that leads back to the actual row. That locator is either a physical row address or, in a clustered table, the clustering key. Because it is a separate structure, a table can carry many non-clustered indexes at once.

scenes.title: Create and use one
scenes.code:
CREATE INDEX ix_orders_customer
    ON orders (customer_id);

-- Uses the index to find matching keys,
-- then looks up each row for total
SELECT order_id, total
FROM orders
WHERE customer_id = 42;
scenes.narration: This index on customer_id lets the engine seek directly to the rows for a given customer. But the query also needs order_id and total, which are not in the index. So for each matching key the engine performs a separate lookup into the base table to fetch those extra columns.

scenes.title: The extra lookup step
steps: Seek the non-clustered index to find matching keys
Read the row locator stored beside each key
Follow the locator into the table (key lookup)
Retrieve the columns not held in the index
scenes.narration: First the engine seeks the non-clustered index and finds the keys that match the filter. Beside each key it reads the stored locator. It then follows that locator into the table, an operation called a key lookup or bookmark lookup, to retrieve any columns the index does not contain.

scenes.title: Clustered vs non-clustered

left.title: Clustered
points: Leaf level is the actual row data
One per table, sets physical order

right.title: Non-clustered
points: Leaf level holds keys plus a locator
May need a key lookup for other columns

scenes.narration: The clustered index keeps the rows themselves at its leaves and there is only one per table. A non-clustered index instead keeps keys and locators at its leaves, you can have many of them, and it often requires an extra key lookup to gather columns it does not store.

scenes.text: Non-clustered indexes make filtered lookups fast, but the per-row key lookup adds cost — index the columns your query returns to avoid it.
scenes.narration: Non-clustered indexes make filtered lookups fast, yet the per-row key lookup adds cost, so including the columns your query returns is the way to avoid that penalty.
